flash-backup.description: Takes about 1-2 minutes: leave the stick in until the screen says DONE -- the screen shows how many MB are copied. Keep the PCM on until then: a copy cut short by the car switching off has to be started again. (It copies in 1 MB writes with the stick set to commit=low for the copy, about 1 MB/s; without bin/fcopy it falls back to cp, 30-40 minutes.) Copies the PCM's whole 64 MB flash (bootloader, system images and /HBpersistence) to the USB stick as pcm_flash.bin, plus the activation file and stored VIN next to it. Read-only -- it is the same read the PCM's own engineering menu does (CustomerService option 05), without needing the menu. Make one before any update or experiment, then check it on a computer with PCM-Explorer (python explorer.py pcm_flash.bin check). Never overwrites an earlier backup; a copy cut short (stick pulled or full) is deleted on the next run and reported; a second copy never runs alongside the first. The file holds your VIN and activations, so don't post it. See guides/RECOVERY.md.

sysinfo.description: Full system dump: takes several minutes, so wait for DONE on the screen before pulling the stick (each finished section is listed in pcm_ran.txt, so an early pull shows how far it got). For a quick VIN and activation check, use the USB Stick tab's Diagnostic mode instead. Comprehensive PCM 3.1 diagnostic. Captures the system log (full + severity-filtered) with boot sequence, boot gates, errors and amplifier detection; the crash record; storage map with partition tables and drive geometry; amplifier resolution (which sound profile is actually live, and whether it matches the flag); odometer and vehicle data; activation codes; software identity and update history; service manager and listening ports; a full restorable /HBpersistence backup; plus the hardware/IPC/CAN/DSI device-tree probe. Read-only -- nothing on the car is modified. Also dumps the DSI service registry from /srv/servicebroker -- the broker's entire live list of registered interfaces and their versions, which no devctl can enumerate -- and the Bluetooth bring-up chain (serfpga, phone-db gate, scp_pss, address-book size, boot-hook and trace-profile presence), which is what determines whether the unit can pick Bluetooth at startup at all.

usb-net.description: Universal ASIX USB-Ethernet driver for PCM 3.1 / MMI3G+ / RNS-850. Supports AX88772 / 772A / 772B / 772C (and 88178 + Linksys/NetGear rebadges) by activating Harman's own AX88772B init path from later firmware. Brings up the link, gets DHCP (or your static address), and enables telnet. 'This session only' loads from USB and never modifies the firmware: a restart undoes it. 'Every boot' (beta, PCM 3.1) also keeps the network and telnet after every restart with no stick, by adding a few small files to /HBpersistence; 'Remove the boot setup' takes them out again.

values.label: Auto adapter · DHCP
values.group: Every boot — stays after a restart (beta, PCM 3.1)
values.note: Every boot adds a few small files to /HBpersistence (never the firmware) and leaves telnet (port 23) and a root shell (port 2323) open, with no password, on whatever network the adapter is plugged into, after every restart. Only use it on a network you trust. Run the stick with the adapter plugged in, so it can tell which driver your adapter needs. To undo it, build a stick with Remove the boot setup.
